events.factual_description: National Sawdust and the Jazz Generations Initiative present Alune Wade & Family Affair / faiith at National Sawdust, 80 North 6th St, Brooklyn, on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Doors are at 19:00 and the performance is at 20:00. National Sawdust describes Family Affair as a new album by Senegalese bassist and composer Alune Wade in collaboration with New Orleans's Neighborhood Story Project, rooted in Afro-Atlantic memory and contemporary dialogue, and states that the album will be released in fall 2026 alongside the documentary TUKKI: From the Roots to the Bayou and the University of New Orleans Press book A Family Affair: Conversations Across the Atlantic. The presenter connects the project to Wade's New African Orleans (2025), framed around West African traditions, contemporary jazz, and Louisiana heritage. faiith is co-billed; National Sawdust describes her as a NYC-raised artist with West Indian roots whose work grows from jazz study and R&B culture. Exact backing musicians for Wade's Family Affair set are not disclosed on the primary event page and are not inferred here. en.why_it_matters: Family Affair turns Wade's bass-led Afro-Atlantic idea into something larger than an album-release set. The Senegal-to-New Orleans conversation is being carried simultaneously through music, a documentary and a book, with the Neighborhood Story Project and Jazz Generations Initiative placing living jazz practice beside memory, migration and community history. Wade's earlier New African Orleans already made the rhythmic connection audible; this Brooklyn date is a chance to hear the next chapter while the project is still arriving.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is already in play on October 13, actively make room for National Sawdust and build the Brooklyn evening around the set. From the DMV, I would pair it with another strong New York reason rather than make a dedicated trip for this date alone.

es.why_it_matters: Family Affair lleva la idea afroatlántica y centrada en el bajo de Wade más allá de un simple concierto de lanzamiento. La conversación entre Senegal y Nueva Orleans aparece a la vez en la música, un documental y un libro, con Neighborhood Story Project y Jazz Generations Initiative poniendo la práctica viva del jazz junto a memoria, migración e historia comunitaria. New African Orleans ya hacía audible esa conexión rítmica; esta fecha en Brooklyn permite escuchar el siguiente capítulo justo cuando el proyecto está llegando.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York ya está en juego el 13 de octubre, sí le haría espacio activamente a National Sawdust y construiría la noche en Brooklyn alrededor del set. Desde el DMV lo combinaría con otra razón fuerte para subir, en vez de hacer un viaje dedicado únicamente por esta fecha.
